name: GDPVal
intro: GDPVal 评估模型能否完成具有经济价值的真实专业工作。它从 9 个美国重要行业筛出 44 个以数字化工作为主的职业，由平均 14 年经验的职业专家编写请求、参考文件和交付物并反复评审。完整集含 1,320 题且不公开，公开黄金集含 220 题；主要评测是盲测职业专家对模型与人类交付物的成对比较。
build_method: 行业与职业筛选, 职业专家出题, 模型辅助筛查, 至少三轮人工评审
metric: 盲测交付物胜/平/负, 更好或持平占比
modality: 文本, 文件, 多模态
task_type: Agent任务, 专业工作交付
eval_feature: 每题三次采样, 三位职业专家盲测, 每题九次比较, 实验自动评分器不替代主指标
scale: 1,320个任务、44个职业、9个行业（公开黄金子集220题）
build_method_en: Sector and Occupation Selection, Occupation-expert Authoring, Model-assisted Screening, At Least Three Human Reviews
eval_feature_en: Three Samples per Task, Three Blinded Occupation Graders, Nine Comparisons per Task, Experimental Automated Grader Kept Separate
intro_en: GDPVal tests whether models can complete economically valuable professional work. It selects 44 predominantly digital occupations across nine major U.S. sectors, then has occupation experts averaging 14 years of experience author and repeatedly review requests, reference files, and deliverables. The private full set has 1,320 tasks and the public gold set has 220; the primary evaluation is blinded expert pairwise comparison of model and human deliverables.
scale_en: 1,320 tasks across 44 occupations and 9 sectors (220-task public gold subset)

drawio_review_note: Reviewed against GDPVal arXiv:2510.04374v1 and openai/gdpval dataset revision 11e7900cdcac61bc4daf59e65feb238acda98fbf; no public official evaluator or automated-grader implementation was found. GDPVal selects nine Q2 2024 U.S. sectors above 5% GDP and 44 occupations after GPT-4o classifies weighted O*NET task share as at least 60% digital. Experts pass interviews, checks, training, and a quiz; fewer than 10% are selected, each has at least four years of experience, and the average is 14 years. They author requests, references, deliverables, O*NET mappings, and realism/value metadata. Model screening is advisory; humans retain control through at least three and an average of five reviews. The full private set has 1,320 tasks, 30 per occupation, averaging about seven hours; the pinned public gold set has 220 rows, five per occupation, with prompt, reference, deliverable, and rubric fields and identifying information scrubbed. Evaluation uses three model samples and three blinded occupation graders, giving nine comparisons per task. Pairwise outcomes are win=1, tie=0.5, loss=0. The main paper reports better-or-tied share, while the appendix speed analysis defines win rate as better-only. The experimental automated-grader service reported 65.7% human agreement versus 70.8% human inter-rater agreement, with 12 of 220 tasks marked ungradable; it does not replace the expert metric.
